Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

## Example 1: Date 2024-10-09

History shows a price rally from ~60 in early October to ~66 by October 9th.
The model forecasts are consistently LOWER than true outcomes.

Looking at the first few days:
- Model: [61.73, 64.50, 64.00, 65.36, 64.77, 63.01, 63.04, 62.42, 61.95, 62.25]
- True: [62.01, 65.00, 64.62, 65.97, 65.09, 63.03, 62.98, 62.28, 61.76, 62.25]

The model is underpredicting by about 0.3-0.6 on average in the first 10 days.
Looking at days 11-20: model is still ~0.5-1.0 below true values
Days 21-30: model is again ~0.3-0.8 below

Sentiment on Oct 9:
[0.00, 0.67, 0.33, 0.00, 1.00, 0.33, 1.00, 0.67, 0.00, 0.67, 0.00, 0.00, 1.00, 0.67, 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 1.00]

High sentiment (1.00) at the end of the sentiment history, but model is still too low.

## Example 2: Date 2024-10-10

This is essentially the same as Example 1, just one day later.
Model forecasts are still consistently below true outcomes by about 0.2-0.6.


The prices have continued their upward trajectory, with the model still failing to capture the full magnitude of the movement. From 62.01 to 68.38 over 30 days, the true outcomes exceeded forecasts by meaningful margins. High sentiment regions correlate with the largest discrepancies, suggesting the model struggles to fully account for market momentum when enthusiasm peaks.
